questions.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_orders
FROM orders
questions.note: This counts every order regardless of status, since order counts include all statuses unless a filter is asked for.

questions.question: How many sellers are on the platform?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sellers
FROM sellers
questions.note: This counts every registered seller in the sellers table (3,095), including any that have not sold anything.

questions.question: What is the average review score across all reviews?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(review_score)::numeric, 2) AS avg_review_score
FROM (
    SELECT DISTINCT review_id, review_score
    FROM order_reviews
) r
questions.note: Each review_id is counted once, and reviews for orders of every status are included.

questions.question: What is the total value of all payments in the dataset?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(payment_value), 2) AS total_payments
FROM order_payments
questions.note: Because the question asks for "all payments in the dataset," this sums every payment row, including canceled and unavailable orders (about 16.01M BRL), rather than applying the sales-revenue status filter.

questions.question: What is the average price of an order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(price), 2) AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items
questions.note: This averages the price of every unit in order_items across all order statuses, because the rules say averages of price are not filtered by status.

questions.question: How many products are there in each product category (English names)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
       COUNT(*) AS products
FROM products
GROUP BY COALESCE(product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
ORDER BY products DESC
questions.note: This counts catalog products in each English category, and products without a category are grouped as "unknown".

questions.question: How many distinct orders used each payment type?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders
FROM order_payments
GROUP BY payment_type
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: This counts orders of every status. An order paid with several methods is counted once under each payment type it used, so the totals add up to more than the number of orders.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders have the status delivered?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) AS total_orders,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') AS delivered_orders,
  ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'delivered') / COUNT(*), 2) AS delivered_pct
FROM orders
questions.note: The percentage is out of all orders, with every status included.

questions.question: What is the average number of installments for credit card payments?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(AVG(payment_installments), 2) AS avg_installments
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card'
questions.note: This averages over every credit card payment row across all order statuses, since averages include every status unless the question asks for a filter.

questions.question: What is the average order value, measured as total payment per order, for orders that were not canceled or unavailable?
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: This divides total payments by the number of distinct orders that have at least one payment row, so the one order with no payment is left out of the count.

questions.question: What is the median total payment per order, across all orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS total_paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    ROUND(PERCENTILE_CONT(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY total_paid)::numeric, 2) AS median_payment,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM order_totals
questions.note: This includes every order status because the question says "all orders", and it leaves out the one order that has no payment record.

questions.question: How many unique customers live in the state of Rio de Janeiro (RJ)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers
WHERE customer_state = 'RJ'
questions.note: This counts distinct people by `customer_unique_id`. Someone who placed orders under more than one RJ address is counted once.

questions.question: How many products weigh more than 10 kg?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_over_10kg
FROM products
WHERE product_weight_g > 10000
questions.note: This counts catalog products with a weight strictly above 10,000 g. Products with a NULL weight are excluded.

questions.question: How many order items cost more than 1,000 BRL?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS items_over_1000
FROM order_items
WHERE price > 1000
questions.note: This counts every order item row whose price, excluding freight, is above 1,000 BRL, across all order statuses, because the question asks about item prices rather than sales.

questions.question: How many delivered orders arrived after their estimated delivery date?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS late_orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
  AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date
questions.note: This counts an order as late when it has status 'delivered', a non-null delivery date, and that date is after the estimated delivery date.

questions.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS sp_sellers
FROM sellers
WHERE seller_state = 'SP'
questions.note: This counts every seller whose `seller_state` is 'SP', including sellers with no sales.

questions.question: How many 1-star reviews include a comment message?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT review_id) AS one_star_reviews_with_comment
FROM order_reviews
WHERE review_score = 1
  AND review_comment_message IS NOT NULL
  AND btrim(review_comment_message) <> ''
questions.note: Each review_id is counted once, and blank or whitespace-only messages are treated as having no comment.

questions.question: How many distinct orders were paid at least partly with a voucher?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS voucher_orders
FROM order_payments
WHERE payment_type = 'voucher'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, because the question asks for an order count rather than revenue.

questions.question: How many products have no category?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS products_without_category
FROM products
WHERE product_category_name_english IS NULL
questions.note: This counts catalog products whose English category name is NULL, meaning the category is unknown.

questions.question: How many orders contain items from more than one seller?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS multi_seller_orders
FROM (
    SELECT order_id
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
    HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT seller_id) > 1
) t
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, since this is an order count rather than a sales question. The result should be 1,278.

questions.question: List the cities in the state of Acre (AC) with the number of unique customers in each.
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city AS city,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
WHERE c.customer_state = 'AC'
GROUP BY c.customer_city
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city
questions.note: Unique customers are counted by `customer_unique_id` (people, not orders), and orders of every status are included.

questions.question: How many orders were approved more than 24 hours after they were placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_approved_after_24h
FROM orders
WHERE order_approved_at IS NOT NULL
  AND order_approved_at - order_purchase_timestamp > INTERVAL '24 hours'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, since this is an order count rather than a revenue question, and leaves out orders that have no approval timestamp.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    oi.seller_id                AS seller_id,
    s.seller_state              AS seller_state,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2)     AS revenue,
    COUNT(*)                    AS units_sold,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id) AS orders
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o  ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue per seller is the sum of item prices without freight, and canceled and unavailable orders are left out, as the business rules require for seller-level revenue.

questions.question: What is the total revenue by customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state AS state,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid), 2) AS revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is what customers paid (SUM of payment_value), which is the default for order-level breakdowns, and it excludes canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which customer state has the highest average freight value per order item?
questions.sql:
SELECT c.customer_state AS state,
       ROUND(AVG(oi.freight_value), 2) AS avg_freight,
       COUNT(*) AS items
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY AVG(oi.freight_value) DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This averages freight over all order items, including every order status, because averages of freight are not filtered by status under the business rules.

questions.question: How many orders came from each customer state?
questions.sql:
SELECT c.customer_state AS state,
       COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY orders DESC
questions.note: The counts include orders of every status, because this question counts orders rather than measuring sales.

questions.question: Which 10 cities have the most unique customers?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    c.customer_city                       AS city,
    c.customer_state                      AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id)  AS unique_customers
FROM customers c
GROUP BY c.customer_city, c.customer_state
ORDER BY unique_customers DESC, city
LIMIT 10
questions.note: Cities are grouped together with their state, because some city names exist in more than one state, and each person is counted once per city using customer_unique_id across all order statuses.

questions.question: What is the average review score of orders paid with each payment type?
questions.sql:
WITH order_types AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT order_id, payment_type
    FROM order_payments
)
SELECT
    ot.payment_type,
    COUNT(DISTINCT ot.order_id)        AS orders_reviewed,
    ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2)      AS avg_review_score
FROM order_types ot
JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = ot.order_id
GROUP BY ot.payment_type
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC
questions.note: Each order counts once per payment type it used, even if it had several payments of that type. An order paid with more than one method counts under each of those methods. All order statuses are included, and orders without a review are left out.

questions.question: What was the total freight charged on items in the furniture_decor category?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'total_freight'
questions.sql:
SELECT
  ROUND(SUM(oi.freight_value), 2) AS total_freight,
  COUNT(*) AS units
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
WHERE p.product_category_name_english = 'furniture_decor'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: I treated total freight charged like a sales total, so canceled and unavailable orders are excluded; remove that filter to include every order status.

questions.question: What was the total revenue from customers in Minas Gerais (MG)?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS mg_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE c.customer_state = 'MG'
  AND o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
questions.note: Revenue here means total customer payments (payment_value), with canceled and unavailable orders left out.

questions.question: What is the English name of the product category 'cama_mesa_banho'?
questions.sql:
SELECT product_category_name AS category_pt,
       product_category_name_english AS category_en
FROM category_translation
WHERE product_category_name = 'cama_mesa_banho'
questions.note: This looks up the name in the category_translation table, which should return `bed_bath_table`.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest average review score among categories with at least 100 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH order_categories AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        oi.order_id,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
)
SELECT
    oc.category,
    ROUND(AVG(r.review_score), 2)  AS avg_score,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oc.order_id)    AS reviewed_orders
FROM order_categories oc
JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT oc.order_id) >= 100
ORDER BY AVG(r.review_score) DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: An order counts toward every category it contains, products with no category are grouped as "unknown", and all order statuses are included.

questions.question: Which 3 sellers have the highest average review score among sellers with at least 50 reviewed orders?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT seller_id, order_id
    FROM order_items
),
seller_reviews AS (
    SELECT so.seller_id,
           so.order_id,
           r.review_score
    FROM seller_orders so
    JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = so.order_id
)
SELECT s.seller_id,
       s.seller_state,
       COUNT(DISTINCT sr.order_id)         AS reviewed_orders,
       ROUND(AVG(sr.review_score), 2)      AS avg_review_score
FROM seller_reviews sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
GROUP BY s.seller_id, s.seller_state
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT sr.order_id) >= 50
ORDER BY avg_review_score DESC, reviewed_orders DESC
LIMIT 3
questions.note: I reduce order items to unique seller–order pairs first, so orders with several units from the same seller are not double-counted. The query includes all order statuses and breaks ties by the number of reviewed orders.

questions.question: How many unique customers bought from a seller located in a different state from their own?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c   ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN sellers s     ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND s.seller_state <> c.customer_state
questions.note: This counts each person (customer_unique_id) once if they bought at least one item from a seller in another state, and leaves out canceled and unavailable orders because the question is about purchases.

questions.question: What is the average price of items sold by sellers in each seller state?
questions.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'avg_price'
questions.sql:
SELECT
    s.seller_state                AS seller_state,
    COUNT(*)                      AS items,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2)       AS avg_item_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
GROUP BY s.seller_state
ORDER BY avg_item_price DESC
questions.note: Following the convention for price averages, this includes items from orders of every status, and each order_items row counts as one unit.

questions.question: How many orders were placed in each year?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS year,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: This counts orders of every status. The 2016 and 2018 totals reflect incomplete coverage: 2016 is sparse, and the data effectively ends in August 2018.

questions.question: Which month had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts orders of every status by purchase month, using `order_purchase_timestamp`.

questions.question: What was the average review score for each month of 2018, based on when the review was created?
questions.sql:
WITH reviews AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT review_id, review_score, review_creation_date
    FROM order_reviews
    WHERE review_creation_date >= '2018-01-01'
      AND review_creation_date <  '2019-01-01'
)
SELECT
    TO_CHAR(DATE_TRUNC('month', review_creation_date), 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    COUNT(*)                                                     AS reviews,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2)                                  AS avg_score
FROM reviews
GROUP BY DATE_TRUNC('month', review_creation_date)
ORDER BY DATE_TRUNC('month', review_creation_date)
questions.note: Each review_id is counted once and all order statuses are included; months after 2018-08 will have few reviews because the order feed ends then.

questions.question: What was the total revenue in Q4 2017?
questions.sql:
SELECT ROUND(SUM(p.payment_value), 2) AS revenue_q4_2017
FROM orders o
JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-10-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
questions.note: Revenue is the sum of payments (payment_value) for orders purchased October through December 2017, leaving out canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: On which day of the week (e.g. Monday) are the most orders placed?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    TRIM(TO_CHAR(order_purchase_timestamp, 'Day')) AS day_of_week,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
GROUP BY TRIM(TO_CHAR(order_purchase_timestamp, 'Day'))
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts every order, whatever its status, because the question is about how many orders were placed rather than about sales.

questions.question: For each purchase month of 2017, what was the average delivery time in days (as a decimal) for delivered orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    to_char(date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp), 'YYYY-MM') AS purchase_month,
    COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
    ROUND(AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (o.order_delivered_customer_date - o.order_purchase_timestamp)) / 86400.0)::numeric, 2) AS avg_delivery_days
FROM orders o
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: Delivery time is the fractional number of days from purchase to customer delivery, counting only 'delivered' orders that have a delivery date.

questions.question: How many orders were placed on Black Friday 2017 (November 24, 2017)?
questions.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2017-11-24'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp <  TIMESTAMP '2017-11-25'
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, because the order-count rules include canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which product category had the largest increase in units sold from January–August 2017 to January–August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2017-09-01'
        ) AS units_2017,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
        ) AS units_2018
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    LEFT JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    units_2017,
    units_2018,
    units_2018 - units_2017 AS unit_increase
FROM units
ORDER BY unit_increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Units sold are counted as order_items rows, excluding canceled and unavailable orders, and the comparison uses the absolute change in units.

questions.question: Which month of 2018 had the most orders?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
    COUNT(*) AS orders
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY orders DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, by purchase date. Data for 2018 effectively ends in August, since September and October have only a few orders.

questions.question: Which 5 product categories had the largest drop in revenue from July 2018 to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_month AS (
    SELECT
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
                  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-08-01'
                 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS jul_rev,
        SUM(CASE WHEN o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-08-01'
                  AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
                 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS aug_rev
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-07-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    category,
    ROUND(jul_rev, 2)           AS jul_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(aug_rev, 2)           AS aug_2018_revenue,
    ROUND(jul_rev - aug_rev, 2) AS revenue_drop,
    ROUND(100.0 * (aug_rev - jul_rev) / NULLIF(jul_rev, 0), 2) AS pct_change
FROM cat_month
ORDER BY revenue_drop DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales, SUM(price) excluding freight, for non-canceled and non-unavailable orders, grouped by purchase month; categories with no name are reported as "unknown".

questions.question: What was the month-over-month percentage change in the number of orders for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-12-01'
      AND order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
changes AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       ROUND((orders - prev_orders) * 100.0 / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS mom_pct_change
FROM changes
WHERE month >= '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: The query counts orders of every status, as the rules say order counts should, and uses December 2017 as the baseline so January 2018 also gets a change value.

questions.question: For each customer state, which product category generated the most revenue?
questions.sql:
WITH cat_rev AS (
    SELECT c.customer_state AS state,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    JOIN products p  ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY c.customer_state, COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown')
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT state, category, revenue,
           SUM(revenue) OVER (PARTITION BY state) AS state_revenue,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rn
    FROM cat_rev
)
SELECT state,
       category AS top_category,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS category_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * revenue / state_revenue, 2) AS pct_of_state_revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY category_revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales, SUM(order_items.price) without freight, because it is broken down by category. Canceled and unavailable orders are excluded, and if two categories tie in a state, only one is shown.

questions.question: What was the 3-month moving average of monthly revenue (the current month and the two before it) for each month from January to August 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-11-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
ma AS (
    SELECT month,
           revenue,
           AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_3m
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue,
       ROUND(moving_avg_3m, 2) AS moving_avg_3m
FROM ma
WHERE month >= DATE '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY month
questions.note: Revenue is the sum of payments (payment_value) on orders that are not canceled or unavailable; November and December 2017 are included only so the January and February 2018 averages cover three months.

questions.question: Which 5 sellers had the highest item revenue in 2018, and what percentage of total 2018 item revenue did each account for?
questions.sql:
WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT oi.seller_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY oi.seller_id
)
SELECT sr.seller_id,
       s.seller_state,
       ROUND(sr.revenue, 2) AS item_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * sr.revenue / SUM(sr.revenue) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_2018_revenue
FROM seller_rev sr
JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = sr.seller_id
ORDER BY sr.revenue DESC
LIMIT 5
questions.note: Item revenue is SUM(price) without freight, excluding canceled and unavailable orders, and 2018 data effectively ends in August.

questions.question: For 2017 and 2018 separately, what were the top 3 product categories by units sold?
questions.sql:
WITH units AS (
    SELECT
        EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp)::int AS year,
        COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
        COUNT(*) AS units_sold
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp < '2019-01-01'
    GROUP BY 1, 2
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        year,
        category,
        units_sold,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY year ORDER BY units_sold DESC) AS rnk
    FROM units
)
SELECT year, rnk AS rank, category, units_sold
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk <= 3
ORDER BY year, rnk, category
questions.note: Units sold counts order_items rows and excludes canceled and unavailable orders. 2018 data effectively ends in August, so that year covers only about 8 months. Ties at third place could return more than 3 rows per year.

questions.question: What percentage of all orders came from each customer state?

FROM orders o

questions.question: Which month in 2017 had the largest increase in orders compared with the previous month?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
           COUNT(*) AS orders
    FROM orders
    GROUP BY 1
),
diffs AS (
    SELECT month,
           orders,
           LAG(orders) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_orders
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT to_char(month, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
       orders,
       prev_orders,
       orders - prev_orders AS increase,
       ROUND(100.0 * (orders - prev_orders) / NULLIF(prev_orders, 0), 2) AS pct_increase
FROM diffs
WHERE month >= DATE '2017-01-01'
  AND month < DATE '2018-01-01'
ORDER BY increase DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: This counts orders of every status, and "largest increase" means the biggest absolute rise in orders. January 2017 is compared with the nearly empty December 2016 (1 order), but it does not win the ranking.

questions.question: For each seller state, which seller has the highest revenue?

WITH seller_rev AS (
    SELECT s.seller_state,
           oi.seller_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    JOIN sellers s ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
    GROUP BY s.seller_state, oi.seller_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT seller_state,
           seller_id,
           revenue,
           RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY seller_state ORDER BY revenue DESC) AS rnk
    FROM seller_rev
)
SELECT seller_state AS state,
       seller_id AS top_seller,
       ROUND(revenue, 2) AS revenue
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue is item sales (SUM of price, without freight) from orders that are not canceled or unavailable, and ties within a state are all shown.

questions.question: What was revenue by state in 2018?

questions.question: How are we doing?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        COUNT(*) AS orders,
        COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS customers,
        SUM(p.paid) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS revenue,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')) AS sale_orders,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
                           AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL) AS delivered,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
                           AND o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS late
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
reviews AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month,
        AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_score
    FROM order_reviews r
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = r.order_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    m.month,
    m.orders,
    m.customers,
    ROUND(m.revenue, 2) AS revenue,
    ROUND(100.0 * (m.revenue - LAG(m.revenue) OVER (ORDER BY m.month))
          / NULLIF(LAG(m.revenue) OVER (ORDER BY m.month), 0), 2) AS revenue_mom_pct,
    ROUND(m.revenue / NULLIF(m.sale_orders, 0), 2) AS avg_order_value,
    ROUND(r.avg_score, 2) AS avg_review,
    ROUND(100.0 * m.late / NULLIF(m.delivered, 0), 2) AS late_pct
FROM monthly m
LEFT JOIN reviews r ON r.month = m.month
ORDER BY m.month
questions.note: I read "how are we doing" as a monthly KPI scorecard for the reliable months (2017-01 to 2018-08), so the sparse 2016 months and the incomplete 2018-09/10 months are left out. It shows orders, unique customers, revenue (payments, excluding canceled and unavailable orders) with month-over-month growth, average order value, average review score and late-delivery rate.

questions.question: Who are our best customers?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_unique_id                      AS customer,
    MAX(c.customer_state)                     AS state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id)                AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid), 2)                    AS total_spent,
    ROUND(SUM(op.paid) / COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id), 2) AS avg_order_value,
    MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date     AS first_order,
    MAX(o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date     AS last_order
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c  ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
ORDER BY total_spent DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I defined "best customers" as the top 10 people (by customer_unique_id) ranked by total amount paid on non-canceled, non-unavailable orders, with their order count shown for context.

questions.question: What was the recent trend?

WITH pay AS (

monthly AS (

questions.question: What is the age distribution of our customers?
questions.sql:
WITH first_purchase AS (
    SELECT c.customer_unique_id,
           MIN(o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS first_ts
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id
),
ref AS (
    SELECT MAX(order_purchase_timestamp) AS ref_ts FROM orders
),
bucketed AS (
    SELECT CASE
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '3 months'  THEN '1. < 3 months'
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '6 months'  THEN '2. 3-6 months'
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '12 months' THEN '3. 6-12 months'
             WHEN r.ref_ts - f.first_ts < INTERVAL '24 months' THEN '4. 12-24 months'
             ELSE '5. 24+ months'
           END AS tenure_bucket
    FROM first_purchase f
    CROSS JOIN ref r
)
SELECT tenure_bucket,
       COUNT(*) AS customers,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2) AS pct_customers
FROM bucketed
GROUP BY tenure_bucket
ORDER BY tenure_bucket
questions.note:
The database has no birth date or age column for customers, so demographic age can't be computed. As a proxy, this query shows **customer tenure**: how long ago each person (customer_unique_id) made their first purchase, measured against the last purchase date in the data.

Customers are counted as unique people across all order statuses, and because the feed ends in 2018-08 (with a few orders in 2018-09/10), the shortest-tenure bucket is slightly understated.

questions.question: What percentage of unique customers have placed more than one order?

           COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS n_orders
    FROM orders o

questions.question: How many orders have a total payment that differs from the sum of their items' price plus freight by more than 1 BRL?

WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
items AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(price + freight_value) AS item_total
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_mismatched
FROM pay p
JOIN items i ON i.order_id = p.order_id
WHERE ABS(p.paid - i.item_total) > 1
questions.note: This counts only orders that have both payment and item rows, across all order statuses, and compares the absolute difference.

  ))::numeric, 2) AS median_delivery_days,
  COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
  AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL

ORDER BY median_delivery_days DESC

questions.question: What was the total revenue from orders that include at least one bed_bath_table item?
questions.sql:
WITH bed_orders AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
    WHERE p.product_category_name_english = 'bed_bath_table'
)
SELECT

    ROUND(SUM(op.payment_value), 2)     AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN bed_orders b ON b.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN order_payments op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')

questions.question: What were the total revenue and the total freight for each customer state?
questions.sql:
WITH pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
frt AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(freight_value) AS freight
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state                        AS state,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(p.paid), 0), 2)      AS total_revenue,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(f.freight), 0), 2)   AS total_freight
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN pay p  ON p.order_id = o.order_id
LEFT JOIN frt f  ON f.order_id = o.order_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY c.customer_state
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
questions.note: Revenue is what customers paid (`SUM(payment_value)`, which already includes freight), and freight is `SUM(order_items.freight_value)`; canceled and unavailable orders are excluded.

questions.question: Which seller has sold to the most unique customers?

FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o    ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
JOIN sellers s   ON s.seller_id = oi.seller_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY oi.seller_id, s.seller_state

questions.question: Which 5 routes from seller state to customer state have the most orders?

    c.customer_state               AS customer_state,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id)    AS orders
FROM order_items oi
JOIN sellers   s ON s.seller_id   = oi.seller_id
JOIN orders    o ON o.order_id    = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY s.seller_state, c.customer_state

questions.question: For each customer state with at least 1,000 orders, what is the average order value (total payment per order)?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS order_payment
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    c.customer_state                                                AS state,
    COUNT(*)                                                        AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(COALESCE(op.order_payment, 0)) / COUNT(*), 2)         AS avg_order_value
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
LEFT JOIN order_pay op ON op.order_id = o.order_id
GROUP BY c.customer_state
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000
ORDER BY avg_order_value DESC
questions.note: All order statuses are included, as the rules say to do for order counts and payment averages, and the one order with no payment counts as 0.

questions.question: By what percentage did revenue in January–August 2018 grow compared with January–August 2017?
questions.sql:
WITH rev AS (
    SELECT
        SUM(p.payment_value) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2017-09-01') AS rev_2017,
        SUM(p.payment_value) FILTER (
            WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
              AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01') AS rev_2018
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
)
SELECT
    ROUND(rev_2017, 2) AS revenue_jan_aug_2017,
    ROUND(rev_2018, 2) AS revenue_jan_aug_2018,
    ROUND(100.0 * (rev_2018 - rev_2017) / rev_2017, 2) AS growth_pct
FROM rev
questions.note: Revenue here means payments (SUM of payment_value), excluding canceled and unavailable orders, with each order dated by its purchase timestamp.

questions.question: What was the cancellation rate (percentage of orders canceled) for each month of 2017?

    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled') AS canceled_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_status = 'canceled') / COUNT(*), 2) AS cancel_rate_pct
FROM orders
WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= '2017-01-01'
  AND order_purchase_timestamp < '2018-01-01'
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1
questions.note: The rate counts only orders with status 'canceled' (not 'unavailable') and divides by all orders placed in that month, whatever their status.

questions.question: For the top 5 product categories by 2017 revenue, what was each category's revenue in January–August 2018?

    ROUND(t.rev_2017, 2) AS revenue_2017,
    ROUND(COALESCE(SUM(cs.price), 0), 2) AS revenue_2018_jan_aug
FROM top5 t
LEFT JOIN cat_sales cs
       ON cs.category = t.category
      AND cs.ts >= '2018-01-01' AND cs.ts < '2018-09-01'
GROUP BY t.category, t.rev_2017
ORDER BY t.rev_2017 DESC
questions.note: Revenue here is item sales, SUM(price) without freight, excluding canceled and unavailable orders, because the breakdown is by category; 2018 stops at August because the data feed effectively ends there.

questions.question: What percentage of item revenue in January–August 2018 came from the 10 products with the highest revenue in that period?
questions.sql:
WITH item_rev AS (
    SELECT oi.product_id,
           SUM(oi.price) AS revenue
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY oi.product_id
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT product_id,
           revenue,
           ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, product_id) AS rn
    FROM item_rev
)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(revenue) FILTER (WHERE rn <= 10), 2) AS top10_revenue,
       ROUND(SUM(revenue), 2) AS total_revenue,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(revenue) FILTER (WHERE rn <= 10) / SUM(revenue), 2) AS top10_pct
FROM ranked
questions.note: Item revenue is SUM(price) without freight, and it excludes canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which product category has the highest percentage of late deliveries, among categories with at least 500 delivered orders?
questions.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT order_id,
           (order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date) AS is_late
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
      AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
),
order_cat AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id,
           COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category
    FROM order_items oi
    JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
)
SELECT oc.category,
       COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.is_late) AS late_orders,
       ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.is_late) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_pct
FROM order_cat oc
JOIN delivered d ON d.order_id = oc.order_id
GROUP BY oc.category
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 500
ORDER BY late_pct DESC
LIMIT 1
questions.note: Each distinct delivered order is counted once per category it contains, and an order is late when it was delivered after the estimated delivery date.

questions.question: How much lower is the average review score for delivered orders that arrived late than for delivered orders that arrived on time?
questions.sql:
WITH delivered AS (
    SELECT
        o.order_id,
        (o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date) AS is_late
    FROM orders o
    WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered'
      AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
),
scored AS (
    SELECT d.is_late, r.review_score
    FROM delivered d
    JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = d.order_id
)
SELECT
    ROUND(AVG(review_score) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_late), 2) AS avg_score_on_time,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score) FILTER (WHERE is_late), 2)     AS avg_score_late,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score) FILTER (WHERE NOT is_late)
        - AVG(review_score) FILTER (WHERE is_late), 2)     AS score_gap
FROM scored
questions.note: This counts an order as late when it arrived after its estimated delivery date, and averages the review rows joined to each order.

questions.question: For each month from January to August 2018, what was the cumulative revenue since the start of 2018?
questions.sql:
WITH monthly AS (
    SELECT
        date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp)::date AS month_start,
        SUM(p.payment_value) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_payments p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT
    to_char(month_start, 'YYYY-MM') AS month,
    ROUND(revenue, 2) AS monthly_revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month_start), 2) AS cumulative_revenue
FROM monthly
ORDER BY month_start
questions.note: Revenue here is total customer payments (`payment_value`) on orders placed in each month, excluding canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Show me last year's numbers.
questions.sql:
WITH yr AS (
    SELECT o.order_id,
           o.order_status,
           c.customer_unique_id,
           o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable') AS is_sale
    FROM orders o
    JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id
    WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2018-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2019-01-01'
),
pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
itm AS (
    SELECT order_id, COUNT(*) AS units, SUM(price) AS item_sales
    FROM order_items
    GROUP BY order_id
)
SELECT
    COUNT(*)                                                    AS total_orders,
    COUNT(DISTINCT y.customer_unique_id)                        AS unique_customers,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE y.is_sale)                           AS sales_orders,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid) FILTER (WHERE y.is_sale), 2)              AS revenue,
    ROUND(SUM(p.paid) FILTER (WHERE y.is_sale)
          / NULLIF(COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE y.is_sale), 0), 2)    AS avg_order_value,
    ROUND(SUM(i.item_sales) FILTER (WHERE y.is_sale), 2)        AS item_sales,
    SUM(i.units) FILTER (WHERE y.is_sale)                       AS units_sold
FROM yr y
LEFT JOIN pay p ON p.order_id = y.order_id
LEFT JOIN itm i ON i.order_id = y.order_id
questions.note: I took "last year" to mean 2018, the latest year in the data. That year is incomplete: reliable data runs only from January to August, and September and October have just a handful of orders. Revenue means payments, and revenue, sales and unit figures leave out canceled and unavailable orders.

questions.question: Which products perform best?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    p.product_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    COUNT(*)                                             AS units_sold,
    COUNT(DISTINCT oi.order_id)                          AS orders,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2)                              AS revenue,
    ROUND(AVG(oi.price), 2)                              AS avg_price
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders o   ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_category_name_english
ORDER BY revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note: I took "best" to mean the top 10 products by item revenue (SUM of price, excluding freight and canceled or unavailable orders), and included units sold and orders as extra performance measures.

questions.question: What will our revenue be next month?
questions.sql:
WITH order_pay AS (
    SELECT order_id, SUM(payment_value) AS paid
    FROM order_payments
    GROUP BY order_id
),
monthly AS (
    SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month,
           SUM(p.paid) AS revenue
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_pay p ON p.order_id = o.order_id
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp >= DATE '2017-01-01'
      AND o.order_purchase_timestamp <  DATE '2018-09-01'
    GROUP BY 1
),
indexed AS (
    SELECT month,
           revenue,
           ((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM month) - 2017) * 12 + EXTRACT(MONTH FROM month) - 1)::float8 AS t
    FROM monthly
)
SELECT DATE '2018-09-01' AS forecast_month,
       ROUND((regr_intercept(revenue::float8, t) + regr_slope(revenue::float8, t) * 20)::numeric, 2) AS trend_forecast,
       ROUND(AVG(revenue) FILTER (WHERE month >= DATE '2018-06-01'), 2) AS last_3m_avg,
       ROUND(MAX(revenue) FILTER (WHERE month = DATE '2018-08-01'), 2) AS last_month_actual
FROM indexed
questions.note: The data effectively ends in August 2018, so "next month" is taken as September 2018. Revenue is defined as payments, excluding canceled and unavailable orders. The forecast is a simple linear trend fitted to the reliable months from 2017-01 to 2018-08, shown alongside the 3-month average and the last actual month as reference points. Treat it as a rough estimate, not a real forecast model.

questions.question: Which product has the most appealing name?
questions.sql:
SELECT
    p.product_id,
    COALESCE(p.product_category_name_english, 'unknown') AS category,
    p.product_name_length                                AS name_length,
    COUNT(*)                                             AS units_sold,
    ROUND(SUM(oi.price), 2)                              AS item_sales
FROM order_items oi
JOIN orders   o ON o.order_id   = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
GROUP BY p.product_id, p.product_category_name_english, p.product_name_length
ORDER BY units_sold DESC
LIMIT 10
questions.note:
This can't be answered from the data. The `products` table has no product names, only `product_name_length` (a character count), and "appealing" is subjective with no measure in the dataset.

The closest thing the data can show is which products customers responded to most, alongside their name length. This query lists the top 10 products by units sold:

This shows popularity, not how appealing a name is, since the names themselves aren't in the data.
